text:
alice: Hey folks — we're getting a bunch of p95/p99 latency alerts for the production inference cluster since ~02:15 UTC. p95 jumped from ~120ms -> ~320ms and p99 is near 980ms. Pattern aligns with last runtime build (runtime-2026-03-14-55) that changed kernel selection to prefer FlashAttention/SDPA by default. :warning:

ben: ugh. is this everywhere or only certain models/seq lengths? any traces yet?

alice: Mainly on long-context chat workloads (seq len ~2k tokens). Shorter seqs unaffected. Traces show heavy time spent in attention kernel, CPU-side stalls waiting for GPU kernel completion. I dug into the build: compile flags include `-DUSE_FLASH_ATTN=1 -O3 -march=native` and a change in kernel selector table (commit 6fb3a2c).

observability-bot: Perf dashboard snapshot: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/attn-regressions/runtime-attn?orgId=1&from=2143209000&to=2143213000 — p95 and p99 panels, flamegraphs attached.

cara: I saw something similar on a dedicated pool yesterday — SDPA path was falling back intermittently to a slower kernel due to bank-conflict heuristics. Could be input size causing an unexpected codepath.

dave: Can we toggle FlashAttention off as a quick mitigation? Is there an env or runtime flag?

ben: Yes — runtime supports runtime knobs. Two options: 1) set REDWOOD_USE_FLASH_ATTENTION=false in deployment env, or 2) force kernel selector to prefer aten sdpa kernels with `REDWOOD_ATTENTION_IMPL=sdpa_aten`. Quick kubectl example:

```
# toggle off flash attention for runtime deployment
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/runtime --container=runtime REDWOOD_USE_FLASH_ATTENTION=false
# or force aten SDPA
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/runtime --container=runtime REDWOOD_ATTENTION_IMPL=sdpa_aten
```

alice: I'm starting a canary toggle now on two pods in prod (zone a) to validate. Will report numbers in ~10min.

deploy-bot: Canary update initiated: runtime-2026-03-14-55 -> env REDWOOD_USE_FLASH_ATTENTION=false on pods runtime-5f7c and runtime-5f7d. Rollout ID rb-21432102.

eva: FYI the compile change also flipped a `-fno-fast-math` flag in the last build? could affect numerics and kernel selection heuristics for certain fused kernels. Not sure if relevant but worth noting.

ben: Good catch. Also the kernel selection code uses a hashed heuristic keyed by (seq_len, head_dim, dtype). If a new kernel mapping got a bad entry that prefers a slower FlashAttention variant for certain head_dim combos, that'll explain the spike. Need to inspect kernel_selector.json in the artifact.

cara: Repro steps I used locally to hit the slow path (linux gpu with recent cuda):

```
# run perf repro (requires container with same runtime build)
docker run --gpus all -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:runtime-2026-03-14-55 /bin/bash -c "python perf_repro.py --model redwood-7b --seq_len 2048 --batch 1"
# curl synthetic load to local runtime
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxx' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":1500}'
```

ben: When you run that, add header `X-Debug-Kernel: 1` — runtime returns kernel selection debug in response headers. That helped me see the selector choosing `flash_attn_v2_slow` for some dims.

perf-bot: After canary toggle, observed p95 -> 140ms and p99 -> 210ms on canary pods. Full prod still had old numbers until we expand. Link: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/attn-regressions/canary-21432102

alice: Nice — can we expand to all pods in that cluster? Also we should create a rollback PR for the kernel selector change and add a unit/integration test to prevent regressions.

dave: I'm doing a rolling env patch now across the cluster. Command queued. Will stagger pod restarts to avoid capacity loss.

deploy-bot: Rolling update in progress: patched env on 6/12 pods. Next batch in 90s.

observability-bot: Post-update metrics: overall cluster p95 back to 150ms, p99 230ms. CPU wait time on host decreased by ~60%.

eva: We should also add a fallback path in runtime: if flash path latency > threshold for N requests, switch kernel impl for that model/route automatically. Filed ticket RW-9157.

cara: Agreed. Also adding a CI perf test that runs the repro with seq_len=2048 against every new runtime image before promoting to prod. Ticket RW-9158.

ben: Follow-up actions for this thread (I'll own):
- PR to revert kernel selector table change (6fb3a2c) -> RW-9159
- Add per-model kernel selection healthcheck and auto-fallback -> RW-9157 (eva)
- CI perf test for long-context workloads -> RW-9158 (cara)
- Add alert rule for attention-kernel-latency regression (p95 delta > 2x) -> RW-9160

alice: Thanks everyone. For now mitigation is rolled out and owners are assigned. We'll keep this thread updated if any oddities remain. :thumbsup:

cara: quick note — please capture the kernel selector json from the bad artifact and attach to RW-9159. I archived a copy at s3://redwood-dumps/attn-kernels/runtime-2026-03-14-55/kernel_selector.json

ben: copied. also adding a small script to synthesize inputs that trigger flash fallback so QA can validate.

alice: closing loop — p95/p99 stable for 45m post-rollback. Moving follow-ups to tickets. If anyone sees a reoccurrence ping this thread.

perf-bot: Regression resolved. Marking incident resolved in Ops timeline. Incident ID: INC-214321. Duration ~1.2hr.

deploy-bot: Rollout complete: all pods patched.

alice: thanks all.
